Relance l’unité aux prochains démarrages: Starts the unit again at future boots.
Interdit le démarrage de l’unité, même à: Forbids starting the unit, even by hand.
Liste les unités chargées, ou seulement: Lists loaded units, or only the failed ones.
Affiche le fichier d’unité réellement ut: Shows the unit file that is actually used.
Mesure le démarrage et vérifie les unité: Measures boot and checks systemd units.
Classe les unités par le temps de démarr: Sorts units by how long they took to start.
Contrôle la syntaxe des fichiers d’unité: Checks the syntax of unit files.
Ancien nom de resolvectl. Les versions a: Old name of resolvectl. Current systemd versions are no longer used that way.
Ancien nom. La commande actuelle est res: Old name. The current command is resolvectl.
Lance une commande dans une unité system: Runs a command in a short-lived systemd unit.
Sets a limit, for example memory.
Écrit un fichier en partant de la derniè: Writes a file starting from the last line.
Writes the lines starting from the end.
Affiche la fin d’un fichier, ou suit son: Shows the end of a file, or follows it as it grows.
Shows the end of the file.
Follows lines as they are added.
Rassemble une arborescence dans une arch: Gathers a tree into an archive, with or without compression.
Change de répertoire pour la suite des a: Changes directory for the following arguments.
Duplique l’entrée standard vers un fichi: Copies standard input to a file and to the output.
Shows the output and records it.
Appends to the end of the file.
Client Telnet. À ne plus utiliser pour u: Telnet client. Do not use it for an administration session.
Teste un fichier ou une chaîne. Le croch: Tests a file or a string. The bracket [ is the same command.
Vrai si le chemin est un fichier régulie: True if the path is a regular file.
True if the path is a directory.
True if the string is not empty.
Measures the time a command takes.
Measures with the shell’s reserved word.
Affiche et règle l’heure, le fuseau et l: Shows and sets the time, the timezone, and synchronisation.
Active ou coupe la synchronisation résea: Turns network time synchronisation on or off.
Arrête une commande si elle dépasse une: Stops a command if it exceeds a duration.
Envoie SIGTERM si la commande dépasse le: Sends SIGTERM if the command exceeds the limit.
Ajoute un SIGKILL si le processus ignore: Adds a SIGKILL if the process ignores the first signal.
Chooses the signal sent when time is up.
Affiche en continu les processus qui con: Continuously shows the processes that consume the most.
Un instantané en texte, sans l’écran int: A text snapshot, without the interactive screen.
Crée un fichier vide ou met à jour sa da: Creates an empty file or updates its date.
Crée un fichier vide ou rafraîchit sa da: Creates an empty file or refreshes its date.
Copies the date of another file.
Remplace ou supprime des caractères dans: Replaces or deletes characters in a stream.
Suit le chemin jusqu’à un hôte et estime: Follows the path to a host and estimates the MTU.
Suit le chemin et estime le MTU, sans êt: Follows the path and estimates the MTU, without being root.
Liste les routeurs traversés jusqu’à un: Lists the routers crossed on the way to a host.
Déclenche une commande à la réception d’: Runs a command when a signal arrives.
Runs a command when the shell ends.
Sets the parameters of an ext filesystem.
Dit si un nom est une commande, un alias: Says whether a name is a command, an alias, a function, or a reserved word.
Répond par un seul mot : alias, function: Answers with one word: alias, function, builtin, or file.
Montre toutes les définitions, dans l’or: Shows every definition, in search order.
Frontal de pare-feu simple, habituel sur: Simple firewall frontend, usual on Ubuntu.
Dit si le pare-feu est actif et quelles: Says whether the firewall is active and which rules are set.
Allows a port or a service.
Affiche ou fixe les plafonds de ressourc: Shows or sets the shell’s resource ceilings.
Shows every limit of the shell.
Masque les droits retirés aux fichiers n: Masks the permissions removed from newly created files.
Shows the mask as granted permissions.
Sets the mask for the rest of the shell.
Détache dès que possible, même si c’est: Detaches as soon as possible, even if it is busy.
Shows the kernel’s name and version.
Version of the kernel that is running.
Ne garde que les lignes qui étaient en d: Keeps only the lines that were duplicated.
Retire une variable ou une fonction du s: Removes a variable or a function from the shell.
Rebuilds the index used by locate.
Rebuilds the database used by locate.
Affiche depuis quand le système tourne,: Shows how long the system has been up, and the load.
Durée depuis le démarrage et charge moye: Time since boot and average load.
Prints the duration in words, procps version.
Crée un compte. C’est l’outil de bas niv: Creates an account. The low-level tool, common to the families.
Crée le répertoire personnel en même tem: Creates the home directory together with the account.
Ajoute des groupes sans retirer ceux qui: Adds groups without removing the ones already there.
Écrit sur une ligne les noms des utilisa: Prints the names of logged-in users on one line.
Who is logged in, on one line.
Édite /etc/sudoers en refusant d’enregis: Edits /etc/sudoers and refuses to save broken syntax.
Résume périodiquement mémoire, swap et p: Periodically summarises memory, swap, and processor.
Une ligne de compteurs à chaque interval: One line of counters at each interval.
Montre les sessions et ce que chacune es: Shows sessions and what each one is running.
Sessions and the command in progress.
Attend la fin d’un processus lancé par c: Waits for a process started by this shell to finish.
Returns as soon as one child finishes.
Relance une commande à intervalle réguli: Runs a command again at a regular interval and shows the result.
Répète la commande à cet intervalle, en: Repeats the command at this interval, in seconds.
Surligne ce qui a changé depuis le tour: Highlights what changed since the previous round.
Downloads a file from a URL.
Cherche le binaire, les sources et le ma: Looks for the binary, the sources, and the manual of a name.
Affiche le chemin d’une commande trouvée: Prints the path of a command found in PATH.
Montre tous les exécutables de ce nom da: Shows every executable of that name in PATH.
Liste les sessions ouvertes sur la machi: Lists sessions open on the machine.
Reads names separated by a null byte.
Limite le nombre d’arguments par lanceme: Limits how many arguments each launch receives.
Compresses a file to .xz, high ratio.
Compresses to .xz and keeps the original.
Ancien gestionnaire de Red Hat. Sur RHEL: Old Red Hat package manager. On RHEL 10 and Fedora 45 it is a compatibility path to dnf.
Crée une archive .zip, lue aussi hors du: Creates a .zip archive, also read outside the Unix world.
Range un répertoire dans une archive .zi: Puts a directory into a .zip archive.
Shell interactif à part, avec ses propre: Interactive shell of its own, with its own extensions.
Compresse vite, avec un bon taux. Format: Compresses quickly, with a good ratio. A common format for recent packages.
Compresses to .zst and keeps the original.
Installe et met à jour les paquets sur o: Installs and updates packages on openSUSE and SLES.
Installe les mises à jour de la version: Installs updates of the current version.
Searches for a package in the repositories.
Comme adduser, addgroup n’a pas le même: Like adduser, addgroup is not the same program everywhere. Debian and Ubuntu ship a script from the adduser package. Alpine ships the BusyBox applet. The other families use groupadd. On Debian, addgroup user group also adds a user to a group: that is then usermod -aG.
Sur Debian et Ubuntu, adduser ada pose l: On Debian and Ubuntu, adduser ada asks the questions, creates the group of the same name, the home directory, and the password. It is a Perl script from the adduser package, on top of useradd. On Alpine, adduser is the BusyBox applet, shorter, and that is the one found on a minimal image. Red Hat, SUSE, and Arch do not install this command: the base tool there is useradd. A script that calls adduser is not portable.
alias nom='commande' fait remplacer nom: alias name='command' makes the shell replace name with command before running it, in an interactive shell. Scripts do not expand aliases unless an option says so. alias with no argument lists them. unalias name removes a shortcut. For something that must exist in scripts, a function is clearer than an alias.
`apk` est le gestionnaire d’Alpine. `upd: `apk` is Alpine’s package manager. `update` refreshes the index, `upgrade` updates, `add` installs, `del` removes. In an image, `--no-cache` avoids keeping the index.
`apt` est le frontal des paquets Debian: `apt` is the package frontend on Debian and Ubuntu. The index is refreshed with `update`. Packages are updated with `upgrade`. `apt-get` remains the stable form for scripts. `apt-key` no longer exists: a repository key is stored separately and cited with Signed-By.
apt-cache search motif cherche dans les: apt-cache search pattern searches the descriptions, show name displays the record, policy name says which version would be installed and from which repository. apt search and apt show cover the same everyday need. apt-cache stays useful in a script, and it has not been removed. It downloads nothing if the local index is already current; otherwise run apt update.
apt-get update, install, remove et purge: apt-get update, install, remove, and purge do the same work as apt, with output and exit codes meant for scripts. apt-get dist-upgrade may remove packages to solve dependencies; upgrade refuses that case. Do not mix the two tools in the same script. For a search, use apt-cache or apt search. apt-get is not deprecated.
apt-key add déposait une clé dans un tro: apt-key add stored a key in a shared keyring: any repository could be signed by any key in that keyring. APT 3, the one in Debian 13 and Ubuntu 26.04, no longer ships the command. A third-party repository key goes in /etc/apt/keyrings, as its own file, and the repository names it with Signed-By. /etc/apt/trusted.gpg is no longer consulted. Ubuntu 24.04 still had apt-key, with a warning; that is no longer true of the 26.04 LTS.
arp -n listait les correspondances IPv4: arp -n listed the IPv4-to-MAC neighbourhood mappings. It belongs to net-tools, no longer installed by default. ip neigh show shows the same cache, for IPv4 and IPv6. ip neigh flush drops an entry when a machine has changed network card. BusyBox may still have arp on Alpine.
ash est le shell POSIX embarqué dans Bus: ash is the POSIX shell built into BusyBox. Alpine uses it as /bin/sh. It knows the common POSIX constructs and some Almquist habits, not the bash language. On a minimal Alpine image it is often the only shell present.
awk lit des lignes, les coupe selon FS (: awk reads lines, splits them on FS (spaces and tabs by default), and runs a program. $1 is the first field, $0 the whole line. NR is the line number. A pattern before the brace selects the lines. On Debian and Ubuntu, awk points to mawk, smaller than gawk. GNU extensions (gensub, IGNORECASE, some arrays) need the gawk package. Alpine ships a BusyBox awk; gawk is installed separately.
basename /var/log/syslog écrit syslog. U: basename /var/log/syslog prints syslog. A second argument also strips a suffix: basename file.txt .txt prints file. For the parent directory, use dirname. In bash, ${path##*/} does the same work without starting a process.
bash is the usual login shell. On Red Hat, SUSE, and Arch, /bin/sh also points to bash. On Debian and Ubuntu, /bin/sh is dash: a script that starts with #!/bin/sh has no arrays, no [[ ]], and no process substitutions. On Alpine, /bin/sh is ash; bash is installed separately. Ask for bash extensions explicitly with #!/usr/bin/env bash.
Ctrl+Z suspend le processus au premier p: Ctrl+Z suspends the foreground process. bg lets it continue without giving the terminal back. Output can still appear on the screen. For a task that must survive the terminal closing, nohup or a service fits better than a plain bg.
blkid écrit le type, l’UUID et parfois l: blkid prints the type, the UUID, and sometimes the LABEL of each block device. blkid /dev/sda1 limits itself to one name. Current fstab files mount by UUID= rather than by /dev/sda1, which can change name across a reboot. blkid needs permission to read the devices, so often the administrator.
blockdev --getsize64 /dev/sdb écrit la t: blockdev --getsize64 /dev/sdb prints the size in bytes. --getsz gives 512-byte sectors, which replaces the old fdisk -s and sfdisk --show-size options. --getro says whether the device is marked read-only. --flushbufs pushes the buffers. This is not a partitioning tool.
brctl show listait les ponts, brctl addi: brctl show listed bridges, and brctl addif added a port. The bridge-utils project is no longer the recommended path: iproute2 provides bridge and ip link. The package can still be installed; it is not in the base system. Old virtualisation scripts still call it; new ones speak ip link.
bridge link liste les ports des ponts, b: bridge link lists bridge ports, bridge vlan shows the VLANs. Create a bridge with ip link add name br0 type bridge, then attach an interface with ip link set eth0 master br0. brctl, from bridge-utils, is the old vocabulary and is no longer the right tool. The package is iproute2, the same one as ip.
btrfs filesystem show liste les systèmes: btrfs filesystem show lists the filesystems it can see. mkfs.btrfs, shipped by the same package, creates the filesystem. btrfs subvolume snapshot takes a snapshot. Btrfs is not the default filesystem of every family: openSUSE and Fedora use it widely, Debian and Ubuntu offer it, and RHEL ships it with a status that has varied across minor releases. Check kernel and family support before putting the system on it.
bzip2 fichier crée fichier.bz2. -d décom: bzip2 file creates file.bz2. -d decompresses, -k keeps the original, -c writes to standard output. tar -j creates a .tar.bz2 archive. The ratio is often better than gzip, and the time longer. New exchanges prefer zstd or xz; bzip2 remains necessary to read archives already published. bunzip2 is the same program under the other name.
cat fichier affiche le fichier en entier: cat file prints the whole file. Several names are concatenated in order. cat feeds a pipe. To read a long file page by page, less is more comfortable. cat -A shows non-printable characters on GNU coreutils. A binary sent to a terminal can leave unwanted sequences there: file lets you check first.
cd est interne au shell : un programme s: cd is internal to the shell: a separate program cannot move the shell that called it. With no argument, cd returns to HOME. cd - returns to the previous directory. A relative path starts from the current directory, not from the directory that holds the script.
cfdisk ouvre une interface plein écran p: cfdisk opens a full-screen interface to create and delete partitions. It writes when you ask it to save. It is the same foundation as fdisk, easier to look at, less suited to a script. Servers without a rich terminal can do without it: fdisk -l and sfdisk are enough.
chage -l user affiche la date du dernier: chage -l user shows the date of the last change, expiry, and inactivity. -M 90 requires a change every 90 days, -E 2026-12-31 closes the account on that date, -d 0 forces a change at the next login. That is not an immediate lock: passwd -l or usermod -L do that. Finer policy also goes through PAM, not only through chage.
chgrp groupe fichier est l’équivalent de: chgrp group file is the equivalent of chown :group file. A user may give a file to a group they belong to, according to system policy. -R descends into subdirectories. To change the owner at the same time, chown is more direct.
chkconfig sshd on créait les liens de dé: chkconfig sshd on created the boot links. RHEL 10, Fedora 45, openSUSE Leap 16, and SLES 16 use systemd: systemctl enable replaces chkconfig on, systemctl disable replaces off. Debian never made it the main tool. Neither did Arch. Alpine uses rc-update. An install script that still calls chkconfig belongs to a previous generation.
chmod 644 fichier donne lecture et écrit: chmod 644 file gives read and write to the owner, and read to everyone else. chmod u+x adds execute for the owner without touching the rest. u, g, and o mean owner, group, and others; a means everyone. -R descends into a directory. The mode of a symbolic link is changed on the target, not on the link itself. chmod does not change the owner: that is chown.
chown user fichier donne le fichier à us: chown user file gives the file to user. chown user:group changes both. chown :group changes only the group. In practice this needs the administrator: a user does not hand their files to someone else. -R walks a directory. --from changes the file only if the current owner is the expected one, which avoids a race in a script.
chronyc tracking dit si l’horloge est ca: chronyc tracking says whether the clock is locked and onto which source. chronyc sources -v lists the servers. It is the time client on RHEL, Fedora, and Ubuntu 26.04, which preferred it to systemd-timesyncd. Debian 13 can still run timesyncd on a simple install: chronyc then has nothing to answer. Alpine often uses it. timedatectl shows the systemd-side result, not the detail of the sources.
chsh -s /bin/bash change votre shell. Le: chsh -s /bin/bash changes your shell. The path must be listed in /etc/shells, or login can be refused. chsh -s /bin/bash ada, run by the administrator, targets another account. The shell that is already open does not change: a new session is required. usermod -s makes the same change without consulting /etc/shells in the same way on every family; chsh is the stricter one.
clear envoie la séquence qui vide l’affi: clear sends the sequence that blanks the terminal display. The emulator’s scrollback can keep the lines further up. This does not destroy data. tput reset goes further and reinitialises the terminal when the display is corrupted.
cmp s’arrête au premier octet différent: cmp stops at the first byte that differs and says where. With no difference it writes nothing and returns 0. -s writes nothing at all and leaves only the exit code. Unlike diff, cmp suits binaries. It does not produce a patch.
column -t lit une table séparée par des: column -t reads a table separated by spaces and aligns the columns. -s: sets another separator. On Debian and Ubuntu the command is in the bsdextrautils package, not in the minimal install of every container. The command remains current. Two options were renamed in util-linux and should no longer be used in a new script.
comm fichier1 fichier2 écrit trois colon: comm file1 file2 writes three columns: lines only in the first, only in the second, and in both. The files must be sorted in the same order, in practice with LC_ALL=C sort. -12 drops the first two columns and keeps only the lines in common. comm does not understand an unsorted file: the result looks plausible and it is wrong.
command ls appelle ls même si un alias l: command ls calls ls even if an ls alias exists. command -v name prints the path or the kind that was chosen, and it is the portable test in a POSIX script: dash and ash know it, whereas which is a separate binary and type is missing from dash. A non-zero exit code means the name was not found.
compress fichier produisait fichier.Z, u: compress file produced file.Z, a format from the 1980s. Current systems do not install it. You still meet it in very old archives. gzip sometimes reads those files through zcat, and the ncompress package, when a repository still offers it, exists only to open them. Compress a new file with gzip, xz, or zstd.
coredumpctl list montre les crashs conse: coredumpctl list shows the crashes that were kept. coredumpctl info PID details one of them, and dump saves it to a file. systemd-coredump must be the kernel’s core handler, which is the case on a usual systemd install. A core is not a fix: it helps you understand a crash. Dumps can contain secrets that were in memory.
cp source destination copies a file. cp -r descends into a directory. cp -a keeps modes, dates, and links, and stays faithful to a tree: prefer it for an administration copy. cp does not copy what it is not allowed to read. On Ubuntu 26.04, cp stays the GNU binary even when the other coreutils come from uutils.
cpio -o crée une archive à partir des no: cpio -o creates an archive from names read on standard input, cpio -i extracts them, and cpio -t lists them. -d creates directories on extraction, -H newc selects the initramfs format. You meet it in boot images and in RPM packages, less often by hand. find . -print0 | cpio -0 -o produces an archive that accepts awkward names. For everyday work, tar is more direct.
Une ligne de crontab est « minute heure: A crontab line is “minute hour day-of-month month weekday command”. The environment is sparse: give paths in absolute form. `-r` erases the whole table.
csplit coupe là où une expression appara: csplit cuts where an expression appears, not at a fixed line count. csplit file '/^#/' '{*}' splits at every line that starts with #. The pieces are named xx00, xx01, unless you change the prefix. It is a GNU tool from coreutils, absent from BusyBox.
curl URL écrit le corps de la réponse. -: curl URL prints the response body. -I asks only for the headers, -o file saves the body, -L follows redirects, -f makes the exit code fail on an HTTP error. -s stays quiet, -S still shows the error. For a simple download with resume, wget is sometimes more direct. curl checks a site only through the TLS certificate: -k disables that check and should not become a habit.
cut -d: -f1 prend le premier champ sépar: cut -d: -f1 takes the first field separated by a colon. -f1,3 takes the first and the third. -c1-8 takes characters 1 through 8, not the visual columns of a wide text. cut does not collapse repeated separators the way awk does. A line with no separator is copied whole, unless -s is set.
dash exécute le langage POSIX sans les e: dash runs the POSIX language without bash extensions. Debian and Ubuntu install it as /bin/sh so that boot scripts stay fast and strict. The other families do not make it their system shell. Writing for dash means writing for sh across the Debian family.
date écrit la date et l’heure selon la l: date prints the date and time according to the locale. A format is given with +, for example +%Y-%m-%d. date -u prints UTC. Setting the clock by hand with date -s needs administrator rights and is now rare: current systems synchronise time with chrony or systemd-timesyncd. date -d is a GNU extension for a relative date; BusyBox does not have it.
dd if=source of=destination lit la sourc: dd if=source of=destination reads the source in blocks and writes them unchanged. bs sets the block size, status=progress shows progress on GNU coreutils. It is used for a disk image or a USB stick. A mistake in of= overwrites the target device with no trash bin. To copy an ordinary file, cp is enough and harder to get wrong.
declare -i fixe un entier, declare -a un: declare -i fixes an integer, declare -a an indexed array, declare -A an associative array, declare -r a constant, declare -x exports. Inside a function, declare makes the variable local, like local. dash knows neither declare nor arrays. For a POSIX script, a plain variable is enough.
df liste chaque montage avec sa taille,: df lists each mount with its size, used space, and free space. -h makes the sizes readable, -T adds the type, -x tmpfs drops in-memory filesystems. df asks the mount, not an unmounted directory. A disk that is 100% full can still accept root writes thanks to ext4 reserved blocks: the Available column is then zero for other users.
diff ancien nouveau écrit les changement: diff old new prints the changes that turn one into the other. -u produces the unified format, the one patch can reapply and code review shows. -r compares directories. Exit code 0 means identical, 1 different, 2 an error. diff -q only says whether the files differ, without the detail.
dig exemple.fr affiche la question, les: dig example.com prints the question, the flags, and the records. dig example.com MX asks only for mail, dig +short example.com keeps only the addresses. @8.8.8.8 queries a specific resolver instead of the machine’s. dig +trace follows the delegation from the root. The package is not always in a minimal image. For what the machine really resolves, getent hosts goes through nsswitch, not only through DNS.
dirname /etc/ssh/sshd_config écrit /etc/: dirname /etc/ssh/sshd_config prints /etc/ssh. On a name with no slash, dirname prints a dot, the current directory. dirname does not check that the path exists. Together with basename, it splits a path without running find.
dmesg montre ce que le noyau a écrit dep: dmesg shows what the kernel has written since boot: disks found, hardware errors, drivers. -T converts the seconds to local time on util-linux, -w follows new messages, -l err keeps only errors. On many machines only the administrator can read the full buffer. This is not the service journal: an sshd failure is in journalctl, not in dmesg, unless it comes from the kernel.
`dnf` installe et met à jour les paquets: `dnf` installs and updates packages on RHEL and Fedora. The index refreshes itself when needed. `yum` is now only a redirect to `dnf`. SUSE uses `zypper`.
doas commande ressemble à sudo, avec un: doas command looks like sudo, with a shorter rules file. permit persist :wheel allows the wheel group and remembers the authentication. There is no direct equivalent of sudo -u in every version: you target a user with -u when the version allows it. Debian, Red Hat, SUSE, and Arch can package doas, but it is not their administration tool. On those families the policy in place is sudo.
dpkg -i paquet.deb installe ce fichier e: dpkg -i package.deb installs that file and fails if a dependency is missing: apt install ./package.deb solves them. dpkg -l lists known packages, dpkg -L name the files of an installed package, dpkg -S /usr/bin/ls the package that provides a path. dpkg-query is the same foundation for selections. You do not update the system with dpkg. It is the low-level tool under apt.
du résume la place utilisée par les fich: du summarises the space used by the files it can read. -s keeps only the total, -h writes it in KB, MB, or GB. -x stays on the same filesystem and does not enter other mounts. du counts allocated blocks, not always the logical size: a sparse file occupies less than the size ls shows. For free space on the whole disk, use df.
dumpe2fs /dev/sdb1 détaille ce que tune2: dumpe2fs /dev/sdb1 details what tune2fs -l summarises, plus the block groups. -h keeps only the superblock. Use it to understand inode size or reserved space before a risky operation. The command changes nothing.
e2fsck /dev/sdb1 est le vérificateur qu’: e2fsck /dev/sdb1 is the checker fsck runs for ext4. -n answers no to every repair and serves as a diagnosis. -p repairs without questions what is unambiguous. The filesystem must be unmounted, or mounted read-only in the case of the root filesystem at boot. -f forces a check even if the filesystem is marked clean.
echo affiche du texte. Son option -n et: echo prints text. Its -n option and the interpretation of \n are not portable: bash, dash, and ash do not do exactly the same thing. For a script that must emit a precise format, printf is the right tool. echo stays readable for a simple message on the terminal.
egrep motif fichier fait la même chose q: egrep pattern file does the same thing as grep -E. Since GNU grep 3.8 the command writes an “obsolescent” warning on standard error, which pollutes cron mail and logs. Current GNU-family versions still ship the name so old scripts do not break, and it should be replaced. BusyBox usually has no separate egrep command: install the grep package or write grep -E.
env sans argument écrit l’environnement: env with no argument prints the process environment. env VAR=value command runs command with that variable, without leaving it in the shell. env -u VAR command removes it for that one run. env is also a portable shebang: #!/usr/bin/env bash looks for bash in PATH.
ethtool eth0 montre vitesse, duplex et l: ethtool eth0 shows speed, duplex, and link. ethtool -S eth0 counts errors and packets. -i identifies the driver. Setting a speed by hand is rare: autonegotiation does better. The interface name comes from ip link. The package is not always installed on a minimal system.
eval concatène ses arguments et les fait: eval concatenates its arguments and has the shell run them. It is rarely necessary. Any untrusted data that passes through eval becomes code: a file name, an HTTP parameter, or a log line can then run a command. When the goal is the value of a variable whose name is computed, arrays or a simple bash indirection are often enough.
exec commande remplace le processus du s: exec command replaces the shell process: there is no return. Scripts use it to become the final program without leaving a shell waiting. exec > file, with no command, redirects the current shell’s output for the rest of the session or the script.
exit 0 signale la réussite, exit 1 un éc: exit 0 signals success, exit 1 a failure. With no argument, exit reuses the status of the last command. In a script, that is the end of the process. In an interactive shell, that is the end of the session. In a sourced function, exit also leaves the calling shell: to leave only the function, use return.
Une variable du shell reste locale tant: A shell variable stays private until it is exported. export places it in the environment of child processes. export -p lists what is already published. Assignment and export can be written together: export EDITOR=vim. Children inherit the value; the parent does not see changes made by the child.
fdisk -l liste les tables sans rien écri: fdisk -l lists the tables without writing anything. Without -l, fdisk opens a menu on a disk: g creates a GPT table, n a partition, p prints, w writes. Current versions of fdisk can handle GPT, not only MBR. For a script, sfdisk is more predictable. Writing a table on the wrong disk erases the partitions. Do not partition a disk that holds the running system without knowing what you are removing.
fg reprend la dernière tâche suspendue o: fg resumes the last suspended or background task. fg %2 targets job 2 as shown by jobs. The task gets the terminal back: Ctrl+C and Ctrl+Z apply to it again. fg does not exist as a separate binary.
fgrep cherche une chaîne fixe, pas une e: fgrep searches for a fixed string, not a regular expression. It is grep -F. The name has been obsolete since GNU grep 3.8 and produces a warning. -F is the right choice when the pattern comes from data and may contain dots or brackets: they stay ordinary characters.
file regarde les premiers octets et la b: file looks at the first bytes and the magic database, not the extension. file image.jpg may answer JPEG, and file binary may answer ELF. -z looks inside a compressed file, -L follows links. -b drops the name prefix, which simplifies a test in a script. The package is not always in a minimal image.
`find` part d’un répertoire, applique de: `find` starts from a directory, applies tests, then an action. The default action is to print the name. Tests combine from left to right. `-delete` and `-exec` really act: check first with `-print`.
findmnt présente l’arbre des montages mi: findmnt presents the mount tree more clearly than mount with no argument. findmnt /var shows the source, the type, and the options of the mount that contains /var. -T file answers for the given file, -S UUID=... looks up a source. --verify checks fstab without mounting. It is the diagnostic command when a path is not on the disk you think it is.
`firewall-cmd` pilote firewalld, le pare: `firewall-cmd` drives firewalld, the usual firewall on Red Hat and SUSE. A change without `--permanent` disappears at the next reload. `--reload` applies what was saved.
free -h montre la RAM et le swap en unit: free -h shows RAM and swap in readable units. The available column, on procps, is the one that says what applications can still use: cached memory is not lost, the kernel gives it back when needed. available is missing from an old free or a very short BusyBox: do not conclude that RAM is gone because free is low and buff/cache is high.
fsck /dev/sdb1 appelle le vérificateur d: fsck /dev/sdb1 calls the checker for the detected type, for example e2fsck for ext4. Do not check a filesystem mounted for writing. -N shows what would be launched without launching it. -A walks fstab. A repair can delete damaged data: work on an image if the data matters. XFS is repaired with xfs_repair, which fsck ends up calling if the fsck.xfs link is there.
Ce n’est pas un binaire. Chaque ligne de: This is not a binary. Each line of /etc/fstab describes a source (preferably UUID=), a mount point, a type, options, then two dump and fsck-pass numbers. mount -a applies the file. A wrong line can prevent boot: check it with findmnt --verify, or by mounting by hand before rebooting. systemd-fstab-generator turns these lines into units on systemd families. Alpine reads them through OpenRC.
ftp hote ouvre une session sur le port 2: ftp host opens a session on port 21. The login and password travel unencrypted, and active mode complicates firewalls. Current versions do not install it by default. To drop files on a machine you administer, sftp or scp go through SSH. curl can still speak ftp:// when you need to query an anonymous public mirror.
fuser /mnt écrit les PID qui ont quelque: fuser /mnt prints the PIDs that have something open under that mount point. -v details the command, -m considers the mount. fuser -k sends SIGKILL to those processes: that is brutal, so look first without -k. Useful when umount refuses with “target is busy”.
getent passwd ada lit le compte via Name: getent passwd ada reads the account through Name Service Switch, so /etc/passwd but also a directory if the machine has one. getent group dev and getent hosts example.com do the same for groups and names. It is the right tool in a script, rather than splitting /etc/passwd, which is incomplete as soon as an account comes from elsewhere. A missing name gives a non-zero exit code and no line.
gpg --dearmor transforme une clé ASCII e: gpg --dearmor turns an ASCII key into a binary file that apt, rpm, or pacman can cite. gpg --show-keys file prints the fingerprint to compare with the one the publisher posted. --import adds a key to your personal keyring, which is not the same as authorising a repository. This entry does not cover mail encryption: it fixes the gesture that replaced apt-key add. The package name varies: gpg, gnupg2, or gnupg.
`grep` écrit les lignes qui corresponden: `grep` prints the lines that match a pattern. With no file, it reads standard input. `-E` and `-F` replace the obsolete commands `egrep` and `fgrep`. Quote the pattern so the shell does not interpret it.
groupadd dev crée le groupe dev avec le: groupadd dev creates the group dev with the next free GID. -g 2000 forces the number. A group is not an account: you put users in it with usermod -aG. On Debian, addgroup is the matching frontend. groupadd fails if the name already exists.
groupdel dev retire le groupe. La comman: groupdel dev removes the group. The command refuses if dev is still the primary group of an account. Files that belonged to that GID keep the number, which ls will then show as a number. There is no option to walk the disk and reassign them.
groups écrit les groupes du compte coura: groups prints the groups of the current account. groups ada asks about ada. The list comes from the primary group and the supplementary groups. A group added by usermod does not appear in an already open session until a new login, or via newgrp for the primary group for the life of one shell.
gunzip fichier.gz recrée fichier et reti: gunzip file.gz recreates file and removes the archive. It is gzip -d. -k keeps the .gz. -c writes the decompressed content to standard output without touching the file, which zcat also does. gunzip cannot open a .tar.gz as a tree: it yields the .tar, and tar -xzf does both at once.
gzip fichier crée fichier.gz et retire f: gzip file creates file.gz and removes file. -k keeps the original, -d decompresses, like gunzip. -l describes an archive without extracting it. gzip -c writes to standard output, which lets you compress a stream. The format is the one tar -z expects. For a better ratio on large files, xz or zstd are more common in 2026; gzip remains the most universal.
head fichier montre les dix premières li: head file shows the first ten lines. -n 20 asks for twenty, -n -5 shows everything except the last five on GNU coreutils. -c limits by bytes. head does not follow a file that grows: that is tail -f.
help cd résume la commande interne cd, l: help cd summarises the builtin cd, where man cd may show something else or nothing. help with no argument lists the topics. It is not the system manual, and dash does not have it. For a binary, man or the --help option remains the project’s documentation.
hexdump -C fichier est le format canoniq: hexdump -C file is the canonical format: offset, sixteen bytes, then the text column. On Debian and Ubuntu it lives in bsdextrautils. hd is often a synonym. For a POSIX tool that is already there, od dumps with a different syntax. hexdump does not modify the file.
history liste les commandes numérotées d: history lists the numbered commands of the session and of HISTFILE, usually ~/.bash_history. history -d N removes an entry, useful for a secret typed by mistake. The !! expansion repeats the previous command and exists only in an interactive shell. Alpine’s ash has a more limited history, specific to BusyBox.
host exemple.fr écrit les adresses de fa: host example.com prints addresses more briefly than dig. host -t MX asks for mail, host 192.0.2.1 tries the reverse name. It is the right tool for a quick check. For flags, TTL, and a comparison of resolvers, dig is more complete. The package is the same as dig.
hostname sans argument écrit le nom cour: hostname with no argument prints the current name. hostname -f tries the full name, which depends on resolution. Changing the name with hostname new does not survive a reboot. On systemd families, hostnamectl set-hostname is the durable gesture. On Alpine, the name is set in /etc/hostname. The package that provides the command is not the same everywhere.
hostnamectl status résume le nom statiqu: hostnamectl status summarises the static name, the pretty name, and the system. hostnamectl hostname new changes it durably. --static, --transient, and --pretty distinguish the kernel name, the one given by the network, and the one meant for people. Alpine has no systemd: edit /etc/hostname.
hwclock lit l’horloge de la carte mère,: hwclock reads the motherboard clock, distinct from the system time that date shows. hwclock --show prints it, --systohc copies system time to the hardware clock, --hctosys does the reverse. Current machines let systemd or chrony handle this at boot. Do not mix a manual setting and network synchronisation without knowing who has the last word.
id écrit l’utilisateur et les groupes du: id prints the user and groups of the process. id user asks about another account. -u keeps only the UID, -g the primary GID, -n the names instead of the numbers. id is the honest test in a script: whoami gives only the name, and it can be missing from a very small image while id is in coreutils or BusyBox.
ifconfig montrait les adresses et, sans: ifconfig showed addresses and, with no option, only the interfaces that were up. The net-tools package is no longer installed on a current Debian, Ubuntu, RHEL, or Fedora. The command can be missing entirely. BusyBox on Alpine still has a short ifconfig: enough for a container, not a replacement for ip. New scripts call ip -br addr.
install -m 644 -D source /dest/fichier c: install -m 644 -D source /dest/file copies the file, creates missing directories thanks to -D, and sets the mode in the same operation. -o and -g set owner and group, which in practice requires being the administrator. Packaging scripts use it instead of cp followed by chmod, so a file is not left for a moment with the default mode.
iostat -xz 2 répète toutes les deux seco: iostat -xz 2 repeats a CPU and disk summary every two seconds. %util near 100 and a rising await mean a saturated disk. The sysstat package is not installed by default everywhere, and its historical collection service (sar) is another use of the same package. The first line is still an average since boot.
`ip` remplace `ifconfig`, `route` et `ar: `ip` replaces `ifconfig`, `route`, and `arp`. Each object has its own subcommand: do not mix addresses and routes in the same form. `-br` keeps the display on one line, `-4` and `-6` choose the family, `-s` adds counters, `-c` colours the output. Nothing `ip` changes is restored at boot: the durable configuration is NetworkManager, systemd-networkd, or the interfaces file. On Alpine these forms come from the iproute2 package.
iptables -L -n -v liste les règles du fi: iptables -L -n -v lists the IPv4 filter rules without resolving names. Current packages install iptables-nft: the command remains, the engine is nftables. The iptables-legacy backend is the leftover to stop using; update-alternatives or the family documentation says which one is active. For new rules, nft or a frontend (ufw, firewalld) is clearer. iptables-save writes the ruleset in the historical format.
iw dev liste les interfaces sans fil. iw: iw dev lists wireless interfaces. iw dev wlan0 link shows the associated network, the rate, and the signal. iw scan starts a scan. iwconfig, from wireless-tools, is the abandoned WEXT tool. Current cards speak nl80211, so iw. Associating to a network day to day is better done with NetworkManager; iw is for diagnosis.
iwconfig montrait le SSID et le signal v: iwconfig showed the SSID and the signal through the WEXT API, withdrawn from everyday use. Current cards and kernels are driven with iw, through nl80211. wireless-tools can still be installed and sees little on recent hardware. NetworkManager remains the way to join a network day to day.
jobs montre les processus que le shell s: jobs shows the processes the shell is tracking: those started with &, those suspended by Ctrl+Z. The number in brackets is for fg, bg, and kill %1. Another terminal does not see these job numbers: they are marks of this shell, not PIDs.
join fichier1 fichier2 écrit les lignes: join file1 file2 prints the lines whose first field is shared. Both files must be sorted on that field, in the same byte order. -1 2 -2 1 chooses other columns, -t: changes the separator. This is not a spreadsheet: an unsorted file produces silent gaps.
`journalctl` reads the systemd journal. With no option, it is the whole journal, from oldest to newest. Options combine a unit, a boot, a priority, or a time range. Without extra rights you see only your own journal.
kill PID envoie SIGTERM, la demande d’ar: kill PID sends SIGTERM, the request for a clean stop. kill -9 PID sends SIGKILL, which the process cannot ignore and which leaves it no time to close its files. Start with TERM. kill -l lists the names. The shell also has a builtin kill, able to target a job with %1. A PID that is not yours needs the administrator. kill does not search by name: that is pkill or killall.
killall nom vise les processus dont le n: killall name targets processes whose command name is name. With no option the signal is SIGTERM. -u user limits to one user, -i asks for confirmation on the GNU version. This is not the same command as on some Unix systems, where killall stopped everything. Check with pgrep name first. On a very busy system the name can be shared by several services.
last lit wtmp et montre qui s’est connec: last reads wtmp and shows who logged in, from where, and for how long. last -n 10 limits the number of lines, last reboot keeps only boots. A system with no wtmp log, common in a container, has nothing to show. last is not the authentication log: failures are in the journal (journalctl or /var/log/auth.log).
lastlog parcourt les comptes et écrit la: lastlog walks the accounts and prints the last recorded login, or “Never”. -u user asks about one account. The information comes from the lastlog file, distinct from wtmp. On a very large directory the command can be slow. It does not list failures.
less fichier ouvre un visualiseur. Espac: less file opens a viewer. Space moves forward one screen, b moves back, /pattern searches, n repeats the search, q quits. less does not need to read the whole file to show the first page, unlike more in some cases. Pipes go through it: systemctl status often starts less on its own when the output is a terminal.
ln -s cible lien crée un lien symbolique: ln -s target link creates a symbolic link: a path to the target, which can cross filesystems and point at a directory. Without -s, ln creates a hard link, a second name for the same file, limited to the same filesystem and refused for a directory. A relative target is resolved from the link’s directory, not from the directory where you type the command.
localectl status montre la locale des me: localectl status shows the message locale and the keyboard map. set-locale LANG=fr_FR.UTF-8 changes the system default language, provided the locale has been generated. set-keymap fr sets the console keyboard. This is not the LANG variable of a single session: it is the setting later logins inherit.
locate motif interroge une base construi: locate pattern queries a database built by updatedb, usually overnight. The answer is fast and can be stale: a file created just now is not in it yet, a deleted file can still appear. -e keeps only names that still exist. The package is not always installed by default. On current versions, plocate has replaced mlocate.
logger -t sauvegarde \"copie terminée\": logger -t backup "copy finished" writes a message that journalctl or syslog can find later, with the tag backup. -p user.warning chooses facility and priority. In a script this is cleaner than an echo into a private file, because rotation and permissions are those of the journal. On systemd the message lands in the journal. On Alpine it goes to the machine’s syslog if a daemon is listening.
loginctl list-sessions montre les sessio: loginctl list-sessions shows sessions, loginctl session-status details one. terminate-session closes a remote session. This is not who: logind also sees sessions without a classic terminal, notably graphical ones. Closing actions need the administrator. Alpine has no logind.
logname lit l’entrée de connexion, pas l: logname reads the login entry, not the effective UID. After sudo, logname stays the user who logged in, while whoami becomes root. With no login terminal, for example under a service, logname fails. It is not a directory of accounts.
losetup -f --show image.img prend le pre: losetup -f --show image.img takes the first free /dev/loop and attaches the file. You can then partition or mount that image like a disk. losetup -d /dev/loop0 detaches it. -P makes the image partitions appear as loop0p1, loop0p2. Forgetting -d leaves the image busy. Current versions create loop devices on demand.
ls écrit les noms du répertoire courant,: ls prints the names in the current directory, or in those given as arguments. -l adds permissions, owner, size, and date. -a includes names that start with a dot. -h makes sizes readable. Order and colours depend on the locale and on LS_COLORS. ls does not descend into subdirectories: that is find or tree.
lsblk lit sysfs et montre l’arbre bloc :: lsblk reads sysfs and shows the block tree: disk, partitions, LVM, loops. -f adds filesystem and UUID, -o NAME,SIZE,TYPE,MOUNTPOINTS chooses the columns. This is not a reading of the partition table in the sense of fdisk: a disk with no filesystem still appears. lsblk changes nothing.
lsmod lit /proc/modules et montre le nom: lsmod reads /proc/modules and shows the name, the size, and the user count of each module. A non-zero count means another module or a device still uses it. lsmod neither loads nor removes anything. For the detail of a module, modinfo; to load it, modprobe.
lsof montre fichiers, sockets et bibliot: lsof shows files, sockets, and libraries held open. lsof -p PID limits itself to one process, lsof +D /var looks for who is using a directory, lsof -i :22 who is listening or talking on port 22. A deleted file that is still open appears as (deleted) and keeps occupying space until it is closed. The command often needs administrator rights to see other people’s processes.
mkdir nom crée un répertoire. -p crée le: mkdir name creates a directory. -p creates missing parents and does not stop if the path already exists. -m sets the mode at creation time, before umask is the only rule. mkdir does not create a file: for that, use touch or a redirection.
mkfs -t ext4 /dev/sdb1 crée un système e: mkfs -t ext4 /dev/sdb1 creates an ext4 filesystem by calling mkfs.ext4. util-linux treats the generic call as deprecated: call mkfs.ext4, mkfs.xfs, or mkfs.btrfs directly. Creating a filesystem erases what was readable on the partition. Check the name in lsblk just before. mkfs does not mount the result and does not add it to fstab.
mkfs.ext4 /dev/sdb1 écrit les structures: mkfs.ext4 /dev/sdb1 writes the ext4 structures onto the partition. -L sets a label, -m reserves a percentage for root processes (5% by default). The command sometimes refuses a device that is already mounted. It does not create the partition: fdisk or parted do that first. For xfs, the sibling command is mkfs.xfs, package xfsprogs.
mkfs.xfs /dev/sdb1 initialise un XFS. RH: mkfs.xfs /dev/sdb1 initialises an XFS. RHEL and the families that follow it often use it for data. You cannot shrink an XFS: you recreate it, or you create a larger one. Repair goes through xfs_repair, not through generic fsck alone. -f forces creation on a device that already carries a signature, which erases that signature.
mkswap /dev/sdb2 écrit la signature swap: mkswap /dev/sdb2 writes the swap signature. That erases the partition’s previous use. Then swapon activates it, and a line in fstab makes it durable. mkswap -L sets a label. A swap file is first created at the right size, then passed through mkswap and swapon. mkswap activates nothing by itself.
mktemp crée un fichier vide dans /tmp, a: mktemp creates an empty file in /tmp, with restricted permissions, and prints its path. -d creates a directory. A template ends with at least three X characters, replaced by random characters. This is the correct way to avoid a fixed name in /tmp that someone else could prepare before you. Pair it with trap to remove it on exit.
modprobe nom charge le module et ceux do: modprobe name loads the module and those it depends on, reading the files under /lib/modules. modprobe -r name removes it if nothing still uses it. Durable options go in /etc/modprobe.d, not only on the command line. modprobe is preferable to insmod, which does not handle dependencies. On many systems loading is automatic as soon as hardware appears.
more est le visualiseur historique, touj: more is the historical viewer, still present through util-linux or BusyBox. It advances with Space and quits with q. It is less comfortable than less for moving backward and searching. more is not deprecated: it is a smaller POSIX tool. For everyday reading, less is the useful reflex.
`mount` attache un système de fichiers à: `mount` attaches a filesystem to a directory, or lists the mounts. A mount started by hand disappears at reboot: the durable line is in `fstab`. `findmnt` rereads the situation more clearly than `mount` with no argument.
mv ancien nouveau renomme dans le même s: mv old new renames within the same filesystem, usually without copying the data. From one filesystem to another, mv copies then deletes. If the target is a directory, the file is placed there under the same name. On Ubuntu 26.04, mv stays the GNU binary. mv does not merge two directories the way rsync would: if the target already exists as a directory, the source is moved inside it.
nc hote 80 se connecte au port et relie: nc host 80 connects to the port and joins the terminal to the socket. nc -l 9000 listens. -v is verbose, -z tests the port without sending data on the OpenBSD version. The name nc hides several programs: OpenBSD netcat, Nmap’s ncat, traditional netcat, or the BusyBox applet. The options -z and -q are not common to all of them. Check nc -h on the machine before copying an example found elsewhere.
netstat -tulpn listait les ports en écou: netstat -tulpn listed listening ports. netstat -rn showed routes, netstat -i interface counters. All of that comes from net-tools, not installed by default on current families. ss -tulpn covers sockets, ip route the routes, ip -s link the counters. BusyBox still provides a limited netstat on Alpine.
networkctl status liste les interfaces q: networkctl status lists the interfaces networkd knows. networkctl status eth0 details addresses and DNS for one of them. If the machine is managed by NetworkManager, networkctl sees the links but is not the one configuring them: nmcli is the tool then. Alpine has no networkd.
newgrp dev démarre un shell dont le GID: newgrp dev starts a shell whose primary GID is dev, if you are a member or if the group has a password. Files created afterwards take that group. exit returns to the previous shell. For a supplementary group that is already active, newgrp is unnecessary: group permissions apply without changing the primary group. sg command runs a single command instead of a shell.
`nft` administre nftables, le filtre de: `nft` administers nftables, the kernel packet filter. Write the rules in a file and load it, rather than stacking commands. On current systems `iptables` is often only a translation toward this filter.
nice -n 10 commande baisse la priorité C: nice -n 10 command lowers CPU priority: the number runs from -20 (most favoured) to 19 (most faded). Without -n, nice adds 10. An ordinary user can only lower their priority, not raise it. nice does not limit memory and does not confine the process. For a service, the Nice= directive of a systemd unit survives a reboot.
nl fichier écrit chaque ligne précédée d: nl file prints each line preceded by its number. -ba also numbers blank lines, which the default does not. -n rz pads the number on the right with zeros. cat -n is more direct when a number in front of every line, blank or not, is enough.
`nmcli` parle à NetworkManager. `device`: `nmcli` talks to NetworkManager. `device` sees the interfaces, `connection` sees the saved profiles. If the machine is configured only by systemd-networkd, those profiles do not exist: `networkctl` and `ip` are the tools then.
nohup commande fait ignorer SIGHUP, le s: nohup command makes the process ignore SIGHUP, the signal sent when the terminal closes. Output goes to nohup.out in the current directory if it is not already redirected. The process can still die with a desktop’s systemd session: for a durable service, a systemd unit or an OpenRC service is the right tool. nohup also does not put the command in the background: add &.
nslookup nom interroge le résolveur et é: nslookup name queries the resolver and prints the address. Interactive mode opens if you run nslookup with no argument. BIND once marked the tool deprecated, then kept it: on current versions it is shipped with dig and host, and it has not been removed. Its output is less stable to read in a script than dig +short. Keep it for habit, not as an exchange format.
ntpdate serveur décalait l’horloge d’un: ntpdate server stepped the clock in one jump. Distributions removed this tool in favour of a daemon that adjusts continuously: chrony, or systemd-timesyncd. A large clock jump breaks logs and certificates. On Debian 13, Ubuntu 26.04, RHEL 10, Fedora 45, Leap 16, and Alpine 3.24, it is no longer installed as a method. If an old document cites it, install chrony and look at chronyc tracking.
od -An -tx1 fichier écrit les octets en: od -An -tx1 file prints the bytes in hexadecimal, without the address column if -An is accepted. -c shows the characters. od is POSIX and present in coreutils. For a more readable hexadecimal dump, hexdump -C is common but comes from util-linux, not from POSIX. od suits binaries that cat would display badly in a terminal.
`pacman` est le gestionnaire d’Arch. La: `pacman` is Arch’s package manager. The full update is `-Syu`. `-Sy` alone, without `-u`, mixes versions and breaks dependencies. Operations are read by family: `-S` installs, `-R` removes, `-Q` queries what is installed, `-F` searches for a file in the repositories.
parted -l liste les disques. parted /dev: parted -l lists the disks. parted /dev/sdb print shows one table. The subcommands mklabel, mkpart, and rm modify it. -s avoids questions, which is convenient and dangerous in a script. parted can resize some tables; it does not by itself resize the filesystem. Enlarge the partition first, then the filesystem with resize2fs or the tool for that type.
passwd demande l’ancien mot de passe pui: passwd asks for the old password, then the new one. passwd user, run by the administrator, sets one without knowing the old one. -l locks, -u unlocks, -S summarises the state. The password is not stored in clear text: the line in /etc/shadow carries a hash. passwd does not change an SSH key. An account locked by ! or * in shadow cannot log in with a password.
paste fichier1 fichier2 écrit la ligne 1: paste file1 file2 writes line 1 of both files on one line, separated by a tab. -d, changes the separator. paste -s puts every line of one file onto a single line. This is not a join by key: for that, join requires sorted files.
patch lit un diff, en général produit pa: patch reads a diff, usually produced by diff -u, and edits the files it names. -p1 strips the first directory level from the path, which almost every project does. --dry-run shows what would happen without writing. -R tries to reverse the patch. A reject is left in a .rej file when the context no longer matches.
pgrep sshd écrit un PID par ligne. Le co: pgrep sshd prints one PID per line. The exit code is 0 if at least one process matches. -a adds the command line, -u user filters, -x requires an exact match, -f searches the full line. It is the usual way to know whether a service is running without splitting the output of ps.
pidof sshd écrit les PID sur une seule l: pidof sshd prints the PIDs on a single line. Unlike pgrep, the name is not a regular expression. -s keeps only one PID, -x includes scripts invoked by their name. BusyBox and procps both have pidof, with options that are not quite the same.
ping hote envoie des échos jusqu’à Ctrl+: ping host sends echoes until Ctrl+C. -c 4 stops after four tries, -W 1 waits at most one second for the reply. No reply does not prove the host is down: a firewall can drop ICMP while the useful port is open. ping -6 or ping -4 forces the address family. On current versions the binary is often capable of both.
pkill motif sélectionne comme pgrep, pui: pkill pattern selects like pgrep, then sends SIGTERM. -f compares against the full command line, not only the short name. -u user limits to one user. -x requires the exact name. This is more precise than killall when several commands share a prefix. The pattern is a regular expression.
pmap PID liste les zones mémoire : code,: pmap PID lists memory regions: code, libraries, heap, stack. pmap -x adds the resident size. Use it to see which library is loaded or why a process is growing. You need permission to read /proc/PID/maps. This is not profiling over time: run it again to compare.
popd retire le sommet de la pile des rép: popd removes the top of the directory stack and moves there. Without a prior pushd, it fails. popd +N removes entry N without necessarily moving there. Like pushd, it is a bash extension.
printf reprend le modèle du printf du la: printf follows the model of C’s printf: a format, then the values. %s prints a string, %d an integer, \n a newline. The format is the first argument; put it in single quotes so the shell does not eat the backslashes. This is the command to use in a script instead of echo -e or echo -n.
ps montre les processus au moment de l’a: ps shows processes at the moment it is called. ps aux, BSD syntax, lists everyone with the terminal and the start time. ps -ef, System V syntax, does the same work with other columns. ps -eo pid,user,cmd chooses the columns. ps does not follow continuously: that is top. The output is not a stable format for a script; pgrep or a read of /proc is.
pstree part de PID 1 et montre qui a lan: pstree starts from PID 1 and shows who launched whom. -p adds the PIDs, -u the users, -s PID keeps only the ancestors of that process. A service that double-forks leaves the tree as a child of its launcher and reattaches to init or systemd. pstree does not replace ps for CPU columns.
pushd /tmp enregistre l’ancien répertoir: pushd /tmp records the old directory on a stack and moves there. popd comes back. dirs shows the stack. It is a bash session tool, absent from dash and ash. In a script, an explicit cd to an absolute path is clearer.
pwd écrit le chemin absolu du répertoire: pwd prints the absolute path of the directory the shell is working in. -P resolves symbolic links; -L, the default, keeps them. It is the reference before a relative path, a script, or an archive.
rc-service sshd status interroge le serv: rc-service sshd status queries the service, start launches it, stop stops it, restart restarts it. The scripts live in /etc/init.d. Automatic start is set with rc-update, not with enable. systemd families do not have rc-service. Alpine service names are not systemd unit names.
rc-update add sshd default lance sshd au: rc-update add sshd default starts sshd at Alpine boot. rc-update del sshd default removes it. rc-update show lists services by runlevel. default is the usual runlevel. It is Alpine’s equivalent of systemctl enable. The other families in this catalogue do not use it.
rcp fichier hote:/tmp/ copiait via le pr: rcp file host:/tmp/ copied through the rsh protocol, in the clear. scp copies over SSH. To keep a tree in step, rsync -aH -e ssh fits better. rcp is not in current systems by default, and putting it back into service is not a goal.
read est interne au shell. Il dépose la: read is internal to the shell. It stores the line it read in the variable you name, or in REPLY if no name is given. IFS splits the line when several variables are named. read -r does not touch backslashes: that is almost always what you want when reading a file.
readlink lien écrit la cible telle qu’el: readlink link prints the target as it is stored, often a relative path. readlink -f follows the whole chain and prints an absolute path; on recent coreutils, realpath does this work with clearer vocabulary. BusyBox provides a shorter readlink.
realpath fichier résout ., .. et les lie: realpath file resolves ., .., and symbolic links, then prints an absolute path. -m accepts a path whose last element does not exist yet, which helps normalise a destination before creating it. It complements readlink -f, with more explicit options on GNU coreutils.
Deux commandes portent ce nom. Sur Debia: Two commands share this name. On Debian and Ubuntu, rename comes from the Perl rename package: rename 's/\.bak$//' *.bak applies a Perl expression. Elsewhere, rename comes from util-linux: rename .bak .txt *.bak replaces the first occurrence of a string. Installing the wrong habit breaks a script copied from a tutorial. ls shows the expected result before you run the command; many versions have a dry-run mode, -n on both, whose meaning you should check with --help.
renice -n 15 -p PID pose la politesse du: renice -n 15 -p PID sets the process niceness. -u user targets every process of one user. As with nice, an unprivileged user cannot make a process more favoured than it already is. The change lasts until the process ends, not until the next start.
reset envoie une initialisation complète: reset sends a full initialisation: useful after a binary that left the terminal in raw mode, with no echo and no newline. It is more forceful than clear. On a minimal Alpine, the command arrives with ncurses; until then, stty sane often repairs the command line.
resize2fs /dev/sdb1 occupe toute la part: resize2fs /dev/sdb1 fills the whole partition. To grow, enlarge the partition first, then call resize2fs, often online on ext4. To shrink, unmount, shrink the filesystem, and only then the partition: the reverse order cuts data. resize2fs does not move a partition and cannot speak XFS.
`resolvectl` queries systemd-resolved. `query` resolves the way the machine does, cache included. `status` shows the resolvers per interface. It is the successor of `systemd-resolve`. Alpine does not have this command.
rlogin hote ouvrait un shell distant dan: rlogin host opened a remote shell in the rsh family. The protocol is no longer acceptable on a network. The November 2026 installs do not set it up. ssh is the direct replacement, with keys rather than an .rhosts file.
rm fichier retire le nom du fichier. Qua: rm file removes the file’s name. When no name still points at the data, the space can be reused. There is no trash bin. rm -r descends into directories. rm -f does not ask for confirmation and does not stop if the name is already absent. On Ubuntu 26.04, rm stays the GNU binary. --preserve-root stops rm -r / on GNU coreutils; do not count on it for an empty variable.
rmdir refuse de supprimer un répertoire: rmdir refuses to remove a directory that still contains a name, including a hidden file. It is the guard when you do not want rm -r. rmdir -p also removes parents that have become empty. For a non-empty directory, use rm -r, knowing what it contains.
route -n displayed routes without DNS. route add default gw ... added a gateway. The command is in net-tools, absent from fresh systems. ip route show and ip route add do the work. On Alpine, BusyBox sometimes still has route. A current install script no longer calls it.
rpm -q nom dit si le paquet est installé: rpm -q name says whether the package is installed, -ql lists its files, -qf /usr/bin/ls finds who provides a path. rpm -ivh file.rpm installs that file and stops if a dependency is missing: dnf or zypper should do the installation. rpm -V checks that files have not changed since installation. Red Hat and SUSE share this low-level tool. It is not the everyday manager.
rsh hote commande exécutait une commande: rsh host command ran a remote command while trusting the source address. No encryption, authentication too weak. Current versions do not install it. The package, when it still exists, is there for an old system that cannot be migrated at once. New scripts call ssh.
rsync -a conserve droits, dates, liens e: rsync -a keeps modes, dates, links, and recursion. -v shows the files, -h readable sizes. --delete removes from the destination what is no longer in the source: useful for a mirror, and destructive if the source is the wrong one. A source directory/ with a slash copies the contents; without a slash, it copies the directory itself. Remotely, -e ssh is the default transport of current versions.
scp fichier user@hote:/tmp/ copie vers l: scp file user@host:/tmp/ copies to the remote machine. The reverse brings a file back. Recent OpenSSH, including those of 2026, carries scp over the SFTP protocol: the old SCP protocol has been removed. The command is still called scp and remains the right reflex for a simple copy. -O asks for the old protocol again, only for a very old server, and that option is not the future. For a synchronisation, rsync -e ssh is more economical. For an interactive exchange, sftp.
sed lit chaque ligne, y applique un scri: sed reads each line, applies a script, and writes the result. s/old/new/ replaces the first occurrence, s/old/new/g replaces them all. -n cuts automatic output, and p keeps only the lines you ask for. -i edits the file in place: on GNU sed, -i.bak saves a copy, and the BSD -i '' syntax is not GNU’s. An expression with slashes is delimited another way: s|/var|/srv|.
service ssh restart existe encore sur De: service ssh restart still exists on Debian as compatibility and ends up calling systemctl. It is no longer the interface to write in a new script: options and unit names read more clearly with systemctl. On Arch, the wrapper is not the documented path. On Alpine, the system command is rc-service, not service. chkconfig, which enabled services at boot on SysV, has been removed from current systemd families.
set -e arrête le script à la première co: set -e stops the script at the first failing command. set -u treats an unset variable as an error. set -o pipefail, specific to bash, makes a pipeline fail if one of its stages fails. set -x traces commands. set -- resets the positional parameters. set with no argument lists variables. These options change the current shell, not a subprocess, unless the script sets them itself.
sfdisk -d /dev/sdb écrit une description: sfdisk -d /dev/sdb writes a reusable description of the table. You can edit it and send it back to sfdisk /dev/sdb to apply it. --list only reads. It is the tool of automated installs. Several historical options were removed from the recommended vocabulary: ask a disk’s size from blockdev, not from sfdisk.
sftp user@hote ouvre un mini-shell : ls,: sftp user@host opens a small shell: ls, cd, get, put, bye. It is the encrypted replacement for an FTP client. get file brings a file back, put sends it. sftp -b commands reads a transfer script. The remote service is the same sshd, sftp subsystem. Do not confuse it with FTP on port 21, which travels in the clear.
sh n’est pas un logiciel unique. C’est l: sh is not a single piece of software. It is the shell the family chose for /bin/sh. Debian and Ubuntu put dash there. Red Hat, SUSE, and Arch put bash there, started in POSIX mode when invoked as sh. Alpine puts ash there, the BusyBox applet. A portable script stays within what POSIX describes: no arrays, no [[ ]], no source in place of the dot.
shopt règle ce que set -o ne couvre pas: shopt sets what set -o does not cover: nullglob removes patterns with no match instead of leaving them as-is, globstar lets ** descend into subdirectories, nocaseglob ignores case. shopt -s enables, shopt -u disables, shopt -p prints the state. dash and ash have no shopt.
shred réécrit l’emplacement du fichier p: shred rewrites the file’s location several times to make the old data harder to read back on a magnetic hard disk. On an SSD, a memory card, or a copy-on-write journalled filesystem, the rewritten blocks are often not the original blocks: shred then does not keep its promise. -u deletes the file afterwards. For a secret on modern media, disk encryption matters more than an overwrite.
sleep 5 bloque cinq secondes. Un suffixe: sleep 5 blocks for five seconds. A suffix s, m, h, or d sets the unit on GNU coreutils and on most BusyBox builds. sleep 0.5 asks for half a second where the implementation accepts decimals. This is not a scheduler: for a reliable repetition, use a systemd timer or crontab.
socat est l’outil général quand nc ne su: socat is the general tool when nc is no longer enough. socat - TCP:host:80 joins the terminal to a port. socat TCP-LISTEN:9000,fork TCP:other:80 relays. The syntax is longer than nc’s and it is the same from one family to another. The package is not in the minimal install. For a simple port test, nc or ss is enough.
sort fichier trie selon la locale, ce qu: sort file sorts according to the locale, which can mix digits and punctuation. LC_ALL=C sort imposes byte order, stable from one machine to another. -n sorts numerically, -h understands sizes 1K and 2M on GNU, -u drops duplicates once sorted, -k2 sorts on the second field, -t: sets the separator. -r reverses. sort -c only checks that a file is already sorted.
source script.sh et . script.sh lisent l: source script.sh and . script.sh read the file in the current shell: the variables and the cd it performs stay in place. A script started with ./script.sh runs in a separate process and has no lasting effect on the calling shell. source is a bash and zsh word. The dot is the POSIX form, the one dash and ash accept.
split -l 1000 fichier écrit des morceaux: split -l 1000 file writes pieces of a thousand lines, named xaa, xab, and so on. -b 10M splits by size. -d numbers instead of using letters. Output lands in the current directory, unless a prefix is given as the last argument. To reassemble, cat in name order is enough.
`ss` lit les sockets dans le noyau. Il r: `ss` reads sockets in the kernel. It replaces `netstat`. The letters combine: `-t` TCP, `-u` UDP, `-l` listening, `-p` the process, `-n` without DNS. `-s` summarises the counters. A `state` filter chooses the connection state.
`ssh` ouvre une session ou lance une com: `ssh` opens a session or runs a command on another machine. The first connection asks you to check the server fingerprint. Durable configuration is in ~/.ssh/config. `scp` and `sftp` use the same service.
ssh-copy-id user@hote ajoute la clé publ: ssh-copy-id user@host adds the default public key to the remote authorized_keys file. It still asks for the password once. -i chooses another public key. After that, ssh uses the key. The command is not a way around a machine you do not already have the right to log into.
ssh-keygen -t ed25519 crée une clé moder: ssh-keygen -t ed25519 creates a modern key in ~/.ssh. A passphrase protects the private key if someone copies the file. ssh-keygen -l -f file prints the fingerprint, which serves to compare the server with what the administrator published. ssh-keygen does not copy the public key to the server: that is ssh-copy-id, or a manual addition to authorized_keys.
stat montre la taille, les droits, le pr: stat shows size, mode, owner, dates, and inode. stat -c '%A %s %n' file keeps only the requested format: symbolic mode, size, name. That is more stable than splitting ls -l. -f asks about the filesystem that holds the file, not the file itself.
strings fichier écrit les séquences d’au: strings file prints sequences of at least four printable characters. You can spot a version, a URL, or an error message in an executable without disassembling it. -n 8 raises the minimum. This is not an analysis: many strings are leftovers, and a binary can have almost none if it is compressed.
stty -a montre les caractères spéciaux :: stty -a shows the special characters: erase, interrupt, suspend. stty sane restores usable settings when Enter no longer returns to the start of the line or keystrokes no longer appear. stty -echo turns echo off, which password readers do. The setting concerns the process’s terminal, not a durable configuration file.
su - ada démarre un shell de connexion p: su - ada starts a login shell for ada, with ada’s environment. su ada without the dash keeps part of the current environment, which surprises paths and the locale. su - with no name targets root. su asks for the target’s password, not yours, unless you are already root. To run an administration command and keep a trace, sudo is the device of the families that install it; Alpine leans toward doas.
sudo commande lance commande en root si: sudo command runs command as root if policy allows it, after your password, not root’s. sudo -u ada command switches user. sudo -l shows what your account is allowed to do. Policy is in /etc/sudoers, which you edit with visudo. -n fails instead of waiting for a password, which is what a script needs. sudo is not a durable shell: the command ends and the rights end with it.
swapoff /dev/sdb2 ramène en RAM les page: swapoff /dev/sdb2 brings back into RAM the pages that were there. If there is not enough RAM, the command fails or the system becomes very slow. swapoff -a targets every area. Do it before deleting a swap partition or shrinking a swap file. This is not mkswap in reverse: the signature stays until the device is rewritten.
swapon /dev/sdb2 active une zone préparé: swapon /dev/sdb2 activates an area prepared by mkswap. swapon -a activates everything fstab marks as swap. swapon --show lists the active areas. Without a mkswap preparation, activation fails. Swap space does not replace RAM: it slows things down, and it keeps a memory spike from killing processes immediately.
sync vide les caches d’écriture du noyau: sync flushes the kernel’s write caches out to the devices. Run it before pulling a stick or after a dd onto a disk. It returns when the kernel has accepted the writes, which is not always the same as an SSD having physically finished. For a stick, umount is the gesture that matters: it syncs and detaches.
sysctl net.ipv4.ip_forward lit une valeu: sysctl net.ipv4.ip_forward reads a value. sysctl -w net.ipv4.ip_forward=1 changes it until the next boot. To keep it, write the key in /etc/sysctl.d/file.conf and reload with sysctl --system. The full list is sysctl -a. These are not service settings: they concern the kernel that is running.
`systemctl` pilote les unités systemd :: `systemctl` drives systemd units: services, sockets, timers, targets. The action is the first word. The SSH unit is called `ssh.service` on Debian and Ubuntu, `sshd.service` on Red Hat, SUSE, and Arch. Alpine does not use this command.
systemd-analyze blame classe les unités: systemd-analyze blame ranks units by the time they took at boot. critical-chain shows the path that delays the most. security unit estimates a service’s exposure. verify checks unit-file syntax. It is not a supervisor: it starts nothing. Boot figures do not compare from one machine to another without the same hardware.
systemd-resolve query nom était le vocab: systemd-resolve query name was the vocabulary of the early systemd-resolved versions. The name was replaced by resolvectl. On Debian 13, Ubuntu 26.04, RHEL 10, Fedora 45, openSUSE Leap 16, and Arch in November 2026, call resolvectl. A script that still invokes systemd-resolve should be changed. Alpine never had this command as a system tool.
systemd-run commande démarre la commande: systemd-run command starts the command under systemd, with a journal and a lifetime independent of the terminal. --uid chooses the user, -p MemoryMax=512M sets a limit, --on-calendar='hourly' schedules. It is the modern replacement for nohup when you want limits and a journal. --user targets your session’s systemd, not the system one.
tac inverse l’ordre des lignes, pas l’or: tac reverses the order of the lines, not the order of characters inside the line. It is the opposite of cat on the vertical axis. To follow a log that grows at the end, tail -f fits better: tac reads the whole file first.
tail fichier montre les dix dernières li: tail file shows the last ten lines. -n 50 asks for fifty. -f stays open and prints lines added afterwards, until Ctrl+C. tail -F reopens the file if it is replaced, which happens when a log is rotated. Several files are followed together by repeating the names.
