`tar` réunit des fichiers dans une archi: `tar` gathers files into an archive. `-c` creates, `-x` extracts, `-t` lists, `-f` gives the file name. Compression is chosen with `-z` for gzip, `-J` for xz, `-j` for bzip2, `--zstd` for zstd. Look at `-t` before extracting.
commande | tee fichier montre la sortie: command | tee file shows the output and records it at the same time. -a appends instead of replacing the file. tee can take several file names. With sudo, the > redirection is done by the shell before sudo: echo x | sudo tee file writes into a protected file, where sudo echo x > file fails.
telnet hote ouvre une session où tout ci: telnet host opens a session where everything travels in the clear. It is no longer a way to log into a machine. The command is still used, rarely, to look at a TCP port’s banner: telnet host 25. Even that use is better done with nc. The package is not installed by default. A remote session is done with ssh.
test -f fichier réussit si le fichier ex: test -f file succeeds if the file exists and is regular. [ -f file ] is exactly test, with a final ] that is mandatory and with spaces. -d tests a directory, -z an empty string, -n a non-empty string, = compares two strings. [[ ]] is a bash extension: it does not work under dash or ash. In a POSIX script, stay with [ ] or test.
Dans bash, time est d’abord un mot réser: In bash, time is first a reserved word: time command measures that command, including a pipeline. The binary /usr/bin/time, package time, adds a detailed report with -v. The two do not have the same options. type -a time shows which one will be used. The time shown splits into real (wall clock), user (CPU in user mode), and system (CPU in the kernel).
`timedatectl` montre l’heure, le fuseau: `timedatectl` shows the time, the timezone, and whether network synchronisation is active. The client behind it is chrony on Ubuntu 26.04, RHEL, and Fedora. Debian can still use systemd-timesyncd. Alpine does not have this command.
timeout 10s commande envoie SIGTERM au b: timeout 10s command sends SIGTERM after ten seconds. The suffix s, m, or h sets the unit; a bare number is read as seconds. Exit code 124 means the deadline was reached. --signal can change the signal, and --kill-after adds a second one if the process ignores the first.
top rafraîchit un écran : charge, mémoir: top refreshes a screen: load, memory, then processes. P sorts by CPU, M by memory, k sends a signal, q quits. -b -n 1 produces a snapshot that can go through a pipe, without the interactive screen. top reads the system at refresh time; a very short spike can escape it. htop is another program, installed separately, and is not part of this entry.
touch fichier crée un fichier vide s’il: touch file creates an empty file if it does not exist, without changing its contents if it does. It updates the modification time. -r aligns the time with another file’s, -d sets a given date on GNU coreutils. touch does not create parent directories.
tput cols écrit le nombre de colonnes, t: tput cols prints the number of columns, tput lines the number of lines, tput setaf 2 sets a foreground colour, tput sgr0 returns to the normal style. Scripts use it to avoid sending raw sequences that depend on the terminal. tput reset reinitialises a terminal whose display has become unreadable.
tr lit l’entrée standard, pas un fichier: tr reads standard input, not a file given as an argument. tr a-z A-Z turns ASCII letters into capitals. tr -d ' ' removes spaces. tr -s collapses repeats to a single character. To replace one word with another word of a different length, sed or awk are the right tools: tr works character by character.
tracepath hote ressemble à traceroute et: tracepath host resembles traceroute and also discovers the packet size that gets through. It does not need to be root. -n does not query DNS. -6 targets IPv6. When the traceroute package is not installed, tracepath is the reflex that is already on the machine.
traceroute hote envoie des paquets avec: traceroute host sends packets with a rising TTL and prints who answers. Routers may not answer, which leaves stars. It is not installed everywhere by default: tracepath, from the iputils package, is often already there and does not need administrator rights. traceroute -n does not try to resolve names, which is faster.
trap 'commande' SIGNAL enregistre une ac: trap 'command' SIGNAL records an action. EXIT runs when the shell exits, INT on Ctrl+C, TERM on a requested stop. trap - SIGNAL removes the trap. Use it to delete a temporary file no matter how you leave. The trap lives in the shell that set it, not in children already started.
tree part du répertoire courant et dessi: tree starts from the current directory and draws the subdirectories. -L 2 limits the depth, -d shows only directories, -a includes hidden names. The package is not in minimal installs. find can produce a flat list when tree is not there. tree changes nothing.
tune2fs -l /dev/sdb1 affiche label, UUID: tune2fs -l /dev/sdb1 prints label, UUID, mount count, and block size. -L changes the label, -m the percentage reserved for root, -c how often checks run. This is not a resize: resize2fs changes the size. You can adjust a mounted filesystem for some options, not for all of them. Read -l before changing anything.
type ls répond par le chemin ou par la n: type ls answers with the path or with the kind of the name. type -a shows every definition, in the order the shell finds them. It is the surest way to know whether you are about to run a builtin, an alias, or a binary. dash, used as /bin/sh on Debian and Ubuntu, has no type.
`ufw` est le frontal de pare-feu habitue: `ufw` is Ubuntu’s usual firewall frontend. It writes the nftables or iptables rules for you. Open SSH before enabling it, or a remote session gets cut.
ulimit -n règle le nombre de fichiers ou: ulimit -n sets the number of open files, -u the number of processes, -f the size of a file that can be created, -l locked memory. The limit lasts for the life of the shell and is passed to children. -H shows the hard ceiling, which only an administrator can raise; -S is the soft limit, the one a user can lower. This is not a permanent setting: to make it durable, set it in systemd limits or in /etc/security/limits.conf.
umask 022 retire l’écriture pour le grou: umask 022 removes write for the group and for others: a file meant to be 666 is born as 644, a directory meant to be 777 is born as 755. umask with no argument prints the current mask, often in octal, with -S for a symbolic form. The mask follows the process and its children. It does not change files that are already there: that is chmod.
umount /mnt détache ce qui est monté sur: umount /mnt detaches what is mounted on /mnt. The name ends with a single u: it is not unmount. The command fails if a process still has a file open or its current directory underneath. fuser -vm /mnt or lsof +f -- /mnt show who. umount -l detaches as soon as possible even if it is busy: the directory empties for new access, and old users finish later. -l is not a substitute for finding the process.
uname -s est le nom du système, en prati: uname -s is the system name, in practice Linux. uname -r is the version of the kernel that is running, not the distribution version. uname -m is the hardware architecture, x86_64 or aarch64. For the distribution name and version, read /etc/os-release. uname -a gathers all of it on one line.
uniq ne regarde que les voisines. Deux l: uniq only looks at neighbours. Two identical lines separated by another one remain. Sort first, or use sort -u. uniq -c prefixes the repeat count, -d keeps only lines that were duplicated, -u keeps only those that were unique. -i ignores case on GNU.
unset nom efface la variable nom. unset: unset name deletes the variable name. unset -f name deletes a function. Without -f, bash may refuse to delete a function if no variable of the same name exists, or the reverse depending on the case: -f and -v remove the ambiguity. An exported variable also disappears from the environment of later commands.
unzip archive.zip extrait dans le répert: unzip archive.zip extracts into the current directory. -l lists, -d /tmp/dest chooses the destination, -n does not replace a file that is already there. An archive can contain ../ paths or absolute paths: -d into an empty directory limits the damage. unzip sometimes asks for confirmation for a name that exists. The package is separate from zip on several families.
updatedb parcourt les systèmes de fichie: updatedb walks the filesystems it is allowed to see and rewrites the locate database. It is usually started by a timer, once a day. Running it by hand in practice needs administrator rights, because the system database is in /var/lib. Excluded paths are set in plocate’s configuration file, not in locate itself.
uptime écrit l’heure, la durée depuis le: uptime prints the time, how long the system has been up, the number of users, and the load average over 1, 5, and 15 minutes. Load counts processes ready to run or blocked on disk, not a CPU percentage. On a four-core machine, a load of 4 can be full employment, not a stall. -p, on procps, prints the duration in words.
`useradd` crée un compte. C’est l’outil: `useradd` creates an account. It is the tool common to the families, the one for scripts. On Debian, `adduser` asks the questions for you. Without `-m`, the home directory is not created. The password is set afterwards with `passwd`.
userdel ada retire l’entrée du compte. -: userdel ada removes the account entry. -r also deletes the home directory and the mail spool. Files elsewhere on the disk, which still carry the UID, are not walked. -f forces even if the user is still logged in, which leaves orphaned processes. Check processes with pgrep -u ada first.
`usermod` modifie un compte déjà créé. `: `usermod` changes an account that already exists. `-aG` adds a group. Without `-a`, `-G` replaces the whole list of supplementary groups.
users est un résumé de who : juste les n: users is a summary of who: just the names, separated by spaces, duplicates included if the same account has two sessions. For the time or the terminal, who is more useful.
visudo ouvre la politique sudo dans l’éd: visudo opens the sudo policy in the editor, then checks the syntax before replacing the file. A mistake in sudoers can forbid every elevation, including the one you would need to fix it. visudo -c only checks. Do not edit sudoers with an ordinary editor. Snippets in /etc/sudoers.d are validated the same way: visudo -f /etc/sudoers.d/dev.
vmstat 2 affiche une ligne toutes les de: vmstat 2 prints a line every two seconds. The first line is an average since boot; the following ones are the interval. si and so are the pages swapped out: seeing them rise continuously means RAM is short. wa is time lost waiting for disks. vmstat does not name processes: that is top or ps.
w reprend who et ajoute la charge ainsi: w takes who and adds the load plus the command each session is running. -h drops the header, -s shortens the line. A session idle for a long time shows in the IDLE column. w does not see processes detached from every terminal.
wait bloque jusqu’à la fin des enfants l: wait blocks until background children finish, then returns their exit code. wait PID targets one process. wait -n, in bash, returns as soon as one of the children finishes. A PID that is not a child of the shell cannot be waited for this way: you need a loop on ps or on /proc.
watch -n 2 commande répète la commande t: watch -n 2 command repeats the command every two seconds and refreshes the screen. -d highlights what changed. The command is reread by a shell: the quotes decide what is expanded on each round. watch stops with Ctrl+C. This is not a scheduler: on disconnect, it stops.
wc fichier écrit trois nombres : lignes,: wc file prints three numbers: lines, words, bytes, then the name. -l keeps only the lines, -w the words, -c the bytes, -m the characters. On an empty input, the count is zero. wc counts newlines: a one-line file with no final newline can report zero lines.
wget URL enregistre le fichier dans le r: wget URL saves the file in the current directory. -O name chooses the name, -q stays quiet, -c resumes an interrupted download. wget -r descends into a site, which can be very wide. For an API or custom headers, curl is more at ease. BusyBox wget does not know every GNU option.
whereis ls regarde dans une liste de rép: whereis ls looks in a list of known directories and can show both /usr/bin/ls and the manual page. It does not walk all of PATH the way which does, and it does not say whether an alias hides the command. Useful to see whether the documentation is installed next to the binary.
which grep écrit le premier exécutable c: which grep prints the first executable that matches in PATH. It does not always see aliases and functions, and it is not POSIX. In a script, command -v is the portable test. On Arch, which is not in the base group. which stays convenient at the prompt to confirm a path.
who lit utmp et montre utilisateur, term: who reads utmp and shows user, terminal, and login time. who am i names this terminal’s session. It is not the list of existing accounts: an account with no session does not appear. Services with no terminal are not there either.
whoami est un raccourci de id -un. Il ne: whoami is a shortcut for id -un. It does not list groups and does not say whether you went through sudo: after sudo whoami, the answer is root. To know who opened the session, look at who or the journal, not at whoami inside a script started by a service.
wipefs /dev/sdb1 liste les signatures re: wipefs /dev/sdb1 lists recognised signatures without erasing them. wipefs -a removes them: mkfs can then start clean, and the data is no longer identified by its header. This is not a secure erase of the contents. Use it when an old RAID, an LVM, or a ghost filesystem stops a new mkfs. Check the device name in lsblk.
xargs lit des mots et les passe en argum: xargs reads words and passes them as arguments to a command. That avoids the length limit of a line the shell expands. With file names, the input must be separated by null bytes, produced by find -print0 and read by xargs -0, otherwise a space or a newline in a name breaks the list. -n limits the number of arguments per launch, -P the number of parallel processes on the GNU version.
xfs_repair /dev/sdb1 vérifie et corrige: xfs_repair /dev/sdb1 checks and corrects an XFS that is not mounted. -n only diagnoses. Do not run the repair on a filesystem mounted for writing. After a hard stop, the journal often replays at mount time; xfs_repair is for when mounting is no longer enough. It is not the ext4 tool.
xz fichier crée fichier.xz. -d décompres: xz file creates file.xz. -d decompresses, -k keeps the source, -c writes to standard output. tar -J produces a .tar.xz, a format widely used for sources and packages. Compression is slower than gzip and the file is smaller. unxz and xz -d are the same operation. -T0 uses every core on recent versions, which matters on a large file.
yum install nom fonctionne encore souven: yum install name often still works because the yum package or a link calls dnf. The options are not all equivalent, and current documentation shows dnf. Writing yum in a new script keeps a name that lost its main role in RHEL 8. SUSE does not use yum: that is zypper. Debian, Arch, and Alpine do not have this command.
zip archive.zip fichier ajoute le fichie: zip archive.zip file adds the file. -r descends into a directory. The archive is not a tar: Unix modes and links are not all kept in the same way. unzip extracts. For an administration backup, tar keeps owners and links better. zip is for exchanging with a system that does not have tar.
zsh n’est le shell par défaut d’aucune d: zsh is the default shell of none of the five families. You install it for the prompt, the completion, and a language close to bash without being compatible with it. A zsh script starts with #!/usr/bin/env zsh. Leaving it as a #!/bin/sh shebang will make it fail.
zstd fichier crée fichier.zst. -d décomp: zstd file creates file.zst. -d decompresses, -k keeps the original, -19 pushes the ratio at the cost of time, -1 goes fast. tar --zstd creates a .tar.zst on a recent enough GNU tar. Debian, Fedora, and Arch packages rely on this format more and more. BusyBox does not provide it: on Alpine it is the zstd package. unzstd is the same tool.
`zypper` pilote les paquets d’openSUSE e: `zypper` drives packages on openSUSE and SLES. `refresh` updates the repositories, `update` applies the fixes of the same version. `dup` changes distribution: it is not the Tuesday-morning command.
